method: Independent manual review of saved answers, actual drafts/verifier feedback and supplied passages; local Corpus byte/hash/outline checks; one isolated deterministic-stub replay of the saved run_turn function. No model/API/backend calls, browser control, production edits or original score changes.
pass_definition: Useful pass requires every original planned task check, independently of the source-verifier flag. Partial value and factual caveats are reported separately.

cases.verifier_failure: Passed an adapted multi-turn loop that omits assistant history, despite the cited complete quickstart containing the required append.

checks.check: Provides a useful Python setup and conversation/turn example.
checks.reason: Provides correct tracing scaffold, but run_turn appends only user messages and returns the model answer without storing it. Unless the opaque call_your_model placeholder mutates history itself, subsequent turns cannot see earlier assistant replies. That hidden side-effect requirement is not stated.

checks.check: Uses the current agent tracing model with correct API names.
checks.reason: Uses the documented current start_conversation/start_turn/start_llm/start_tool API names and nesting; source S5 shows the full pattern.

checks.check: Does not claim an unexecuted SDK example was run.
checks.reason: Explicitly says the example was not run; no agent execution action is recorded.

repair_chronology.reason: Only draft passed. The verifier checked API names/nesting but did not flag the missing assistant-history append.

findings.source_evidence: The full quickstart appends the first assistant message via msg.model_dump(exclude_none=True), and the final assistant reply via history.append({role: assistant, content: msg.content}).
findings.answer_evidence: The adapted run_turn only appends {role: user, content: user_message}; llm.output(answer) records tracing output and is not an append to the local history list.
findings.assessment: This bug was caught and repaired in v2, then recurred and passed in v3. The observed difference does not establish prompt causation; it demonstrates verifier variability on a real semantic issue.

The trailing note about unread manual lifecycle/semantic-convention sections does not help the requested task. Optional quickstart package/integration guidance makes the answer longer than the requested core pattern.

offline_reproduction.method: Extracted only the saved run_turn AST and executed it with inert context managers plus a deterministic pure call_your_model stub. Did not execute imports, weave.init, top-level snippet, actual SDK spans or provider calls.
offline_reproduction.stub_side_effects: Returns a fixed assistant string and captures a deep copy of supplied history; does not mutate history.
offline_reproduction.limit: A user-supplied placeholder could deliberately mutate history, but the example neither implements nor documents that responsibility.

checks.check: Explains stable conversation_id reuse in the prior Python context.
checks.reason: Explains stable conversation_id reuse and shows generating/storing it on the first request, then passing the saved value on a later request. Source S7 expressly states that same-ID reuse adds turns to an existing conversation.

checks.check: Does not imply metadata alone stores user chat history or grants persistence.
checks.reason: Describes persistence of the ID in application chat state and grouping of trace turns; never claims this restores the model message history or arbitrary application state. It could explain the distinction more directly but does not imply automatic restoration.

checks.check: Uses supported APIs or clearly states evidence limits.
checks.reason: After a source-specific first rejection, it reads S9 for the returned conversation_id attribute and context-manager usage, plus S10 for instance start_turn. Final API usage is supported; it explicitly labels the example unexecuted and per-request recommendation as inference.

repair_chronology.reason: Draft cited S7 for returned object attribute/context-manager usage absent from that passage, relied on an uncited turn API, and made stronger assertions about arbitrary string IDs and per-request setup than the narrow cited evidence.
Read quickstart section10 (S9) and tracing section5 (S10), adding the missing API evidence.
Final code uses saved generated ID and documented instance method, with the added API sources cited.

findings.assessment: Unlike a wording-only repair, the second draft follows two new relevant reads supplying the attribute and method evidence needed for the final example.

Caveats about arbitrary application IDs, concurrent turns and changed agent_name are not needed to answer preserving an existing conversation. The core approach remains useful. Source S7 already invites supplied stable IDs; saving a generated ID is valid but not demonstrated to be intrinsically safer than an application ID.

cases.comparison_to_v2: Still delivers correct stable-ID guidance but takes an additional research/repair cycle and adds longer caveats. These selected executions are not an efficiency benchmark.

limits: Two selected questions in one conversation, one execution each; no causal inference about prompt changes or population accuracy.
The isolated stub replay establishes local history-list behavior under a nonmutating model wrapper, not end-to-end SDK/provider behavior.
Support mode does not guarantee code completeness; the supplied S5 evidence had the missing history append.
Original drafts, audit verdicts and scores remain untouched.
